items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The Ben Webster story where he’s doing a record of ballads... He says, 'yeah, man, I forgot the words.'

ctx.x: Yeah, you said that, I know you said that, “some of my biggest influences are sax players.”

Yeah. You know let me reiterate another story. I mean these are stories that we probably know. The Ben Webster story where he’s doing a record of ballads. And he’s one take right after the other. One take, that’s a take, okay next. Next take. They get to like the fifth tune and they’re playing and Ben just stops. So everybody stops and the engineer says, “Ben, is there a problem?” He says, “yeah, man, I forgot the words.” He’s playing a tenor. “Yeah but I forgot the words.” So it’s important to tell a story and…
All right. I won’t expect that from you. Maybe you could describe someone else who’s feeling pretty and put that spin on it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
